items.title: The Fate of Somalia: Assessing the Consequences of Executive Overreach and Constitutional Crisis
items.description: By Djama Mahamoud Ali Under President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud, a pattern of executive actions that have systematically undermined federalism, regional autonomy, and constitutional governance have become normal. This pattern include interference in South West State elections, the coerced resignation of Galmudug’s president, military confrontation with Jubaland, the deployment of forces against Puntland, and unilateral constitutional changes. this analysis assesses the likely trajectory of Somalia’s fragile statehood. The cumulative effect of these actions, combined with the opposition’s unified rejection of the president’s agenda, points toward a deepening political fragmentation that risks reversing the modest gains achieved since the establishment of the federal system in 2012. Since his re-election in 2022, President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud has pursued an ambitious agenda of centralizing authority in Mogadishu. While framed as state-building and democratic reform, this agenda has precipitated a profound crisis in Somalia’s federal system. The President’s approach, characterized by unilateral actions against federal member states contested constitutional amendments, and the prioritization of political consolidation over counterterrorism, has generated unprecedented resistance from regional administrations and opposition coalitions. This paper assesses the fate of Somalia by examining a series of interconnected crises that, together, threaten the country’s political cohesion.   A Pattern of Electoral Manipulation The President’s conduct in South West State established a troubling template for federal intervention in regional affairs. When the President of the South West State was ousted, Hassan Sheikh Mohamud appointed an interim president, a move that violated both the federal constitution and the South West State’s own governing charter. More significantly, he proceeded to appoint the very individual who would win the pre-fixed election he was organizing in Baydhabo. As foreseen Aden Madobe became the President of the South West State. The pattern established in South West State was replicated in Galmudug, where President Mohamud forced the sitting president to resign and subsequently appointed his replacement. This intervention, like that in South West State, violated the principles of federal autonomy enshrined in Somalia’s provisional constitution. The President’s willingness to unilaterally remove and replace regional leaders demonstrates a fundamental disregard for the federal structure that was designed to prevent the concentration of power in Mogadishu. The cumulative effect of these interventions has been the erosion of trust between the federal government and federal member states. As one analysis noted, “President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud’s ambitious drive to centralize authority has collided with the entrenched realities of Somalia’s decentralized political landscape.” To control the outcome of the elections, Hassan Sh. is employing a classic “stick and carrot” strategy:  The stick is the use of military force and federal security pressure to coerce federal member states into compliance. This includes interventions such as ousting sitting administrations, imposing interim appointments, and direct assaults to overturn regional leaders who resist his agenda, as seen in South West State, Galmudug, and the attempted move against Jubaland. The carrot is the use of financial inducements and political appointments to co-opt the opposition. By offering money, positions, or favorable electoral terms, he seeks to neutralize resistance and secure acquiescence from rival candidates and power brokers without open confrontation. Together, these two tactics are designed to eliminate genuine competition and engineer a political environment in which his preferred outcome in Baydhabo and elsewhere is effectively predetermined   Military Failure and Regional Resistance The most dramatic illustration of the President’s confrontational approach came in Jubaland. When Jubaland proceeded with its presidential election in early 2024, defying Mogadishu, the federal government declared the re-election of Ahmed Madobe il-legal. The standoff escalated dramatically: the federal government issued an arrest warrant for Madobe, accused him of collaborating with Al-Shabaab, and launched a military operation in the Ras Kamboni area in an attempt to take control of Kismayo. The military operation ended in failure, with federal troops retreating across the Kenyan border. Mogadishu subsequently imposed an air blockade on Kismayo. Jubaland further accused President Mohamud of orchestrating coordinated attacks on the towns of Balad Hawo and Doolow in the Gedo region, warning that the federal government’s actions threaten to destabilize the country’s fragile security landscape as Al-Shabaab militants make territorial gains. Jubaland’s administration described the attacks as a deliberate attempt to spark a broader conflict in the region and declared its commitment to resisting any illegitimate plans by Hassan Sheikh Mohamud. The military defeat in Jubaland was a significant blow to the President’s authority. By late 2025, the confrontation had forced a retreat to foreign-mediated dialogue, with Kenya brokering talks between Hassan Sheikh and Madobe. This marked a public acknowledgment that unilateral governance has failed.   From Neglect to Military Confrontation The relationship between the federal government and Puntland has deteriorated to the point of near-severance. This crisis has two interrelated dimensions: the federal government’s refusal to support Puntland’s counterterrorism efforts, and the President’s current military buildup aimed at overthrowing the Puntland administration. While Puntland has been engaged in Operation Hilaac, a months-long offensive against ISIS militants in the Al Miskaad mountains, the federal government has been accused of undermining rather than supporting these efforts. Puntland’s Ministry of Information stated: “Somali Federal Government is destabilizing peace in Puntland state of Somalia causing unrest while Puntland state is waging war against ISIS and Al Shabaab. Hasan sheikh is trying to prevent Puntland victory and defeat international Terrorists.” Documented evidence supports these accusations. The federal government reportedly invested hundreds of thousands of US Dollars in arming militias to destabilize Puntland. These funds were diverted from counter-terrorism to fuel clan conflicts in one of Somalia’s most stable regions. Furthermore, the federal government allegedly refused clearance for planes seeking to transport Puntland’s wounded soldiers, effectively denying medical evacuation for forces fighting ISIS. The President is currently massing military forces against Puntland in an attempt to overthrow State President Said Abdullahi Deni. This follows Puntland’s unprecedented declaration of administrative independence in response to the March 2024 constitutional amendments. Since then, Puntland has suspended cooperation with the federal government. Centralization Disguised as Reform The underlying driver of these regional confrontations has been the President’s push for constitutional amendments. In March 2024, the federal government rushed through constitutional changes that were widely perceived as a move to concentrate power in Villa Somalia and were enacted without national consensus. The amendments were swiftly rejected by Puntland and Jubaland as well as the opposition Somali Salvation Forum, who accused President Hassan of corruption, human rights abuses, and unconstitutional amendments that expanded presidential powers. Critics argue the reforms were rushed and not inclusive, with Puntland and Jubaland insisting that the process did not follow the proper path. President Mohamud has defended the amendments, arguing that lawmakers had the authority to amend agreements reached with federal member states. The constitution is not the Quran, he stated. However, opponents contend the reforms were designed to consolidate executive dominance ahead of elections rather than strengthen democracy. Conclusion President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud’s tenure has been characterized by a consistent pattern of executive overreach: manipulating elections in South West State, forcing the resignation of Galmudug’s president, launching a failed military campaign against Jubaland, massing forces against Puntland while withholding support for its counterterrorism efforts, and pushing through constitutional amendments without national consensus. These actions have unified the opposition and alienated federal member states to an unprecedented degree. The fate of Somalia hangs in the balance. If the President continues on his current path, the country faces the prospect of deepening fragmentation, security deterioration, and constitutional crisis. A return to the chaos of the 1990s, as Puntland’s Vice President warned, is a real possibility. Alternatively, if the President embraces genuine consensus politics and accepts a recalibration of federal power, Somalia may yet salvage its fragile state-building project. The choice, as one analysis put it, is between “genuine recalibration of federal power and embrace consensus politics” or “presiding over the irreversible disintegration” of the nation. The coming months will be decisive in determining which path Somalia takes. items.title: Friday Sermons Rally Puntland as Tensions Rise Over Alleged Federal Military Activities
items.description: Garowe (WDN) – Friday prayers across Puntland’s capital, Garowe, became a platform for calls to safeguard the region’s security and political stability as tensions continue to mount over allegations that Somalia’s Federal Government is seeking to undermine Puntland through military deployments and weapons transfers. Imams and religious scholars used their weekly sermons to urge residents to remain united in defense of Puntland’s peace, warning against what they described as attempts to destabilize one of Somalia’s most stable federal member states. The increasingly vocal response from Puntland’s religious leaders reflects the growing public anxiety over the unfolding crisis. By addressing the issue from mosque pulpits, they have elevated the dispute beyond politics, framing the preservation of Puntland’s peace and stability as both a civic and moral obligation. The clerics called on the public to reject any actions or actors they believe threaten Puntland’s security, emphasizing that preserving peace and constitutional order should remain a collective responsibility. The sermons come amid an escalating political confrontation between the Puntland administration and the Federal Government in Mogadishu. President Said Abdullahi Deni who facing a mounting allegations of maladministration, abuse of power and corruption, has accused the Federal Government of pursuing a unilateral campaign aimed at weakening Puntland’s institutions. Puntland officials allege that Mogadishu has been organizing armed groups and facilitating the movement of weapons into parts of Puntland without the consent of the regional authorities—claims the Federal Government has not publicly addressed. According to Puntland officials, the Mudug region has become a particular focus of concern, with reports of increased federal military activity fueling fears of further escalation. The Puntland government has vowed to take what it describes as appropriate measures to protect the region’s security and constitutional authority. The dispute marks the latest chapter in the deepening political rift between Puntland and the Federal Government, whose relations have deteriorated sharply over disagreements concerning constitutional reforms, electoral arrangements, federal-state powers, and governance. The meddling and interference of Villa Somalia to alter the balance of power inside Puntland without broad political consensus risks inflaming an already fragile relationship between Mogadishu and one of the country’s most influential federal member states. As accusations and counteraccusations continue to intensify, concerns are mounting that Somalia’s unresolved political disputes could further strain relations between the Federal Government and Puntland unless addressed through dialogue and constitutional mechanisms rather than confrontation. By addressing the issue from mosque pulpits, they have elevated the dispute beyond politics, framing the preservation of Puntland’s peace and stability as both a civic and moral obligation. The clerics called on the public to reject any actions or actors they believe threaten Puntland’s security, emphasizing that preserving peace and constitutional order should remain a collective responsibility. The sermons come amid an escalating political confrontation between the Puntland administration and the Federal Government in Mogadishu. President Said Abdullahi Deni who facing a mounting allegations of maladministration, abuse of power and corruption, has accused the Federal Government of pursuing a unilateral campaign aimed at weakening Puntland’s institutions. Puntland officials allege that Mogadishu has been organizing armed groups and facilitating the movement of weapons into parts of Puntland without the consent of the regional authorities—claims the Federal Government has not publicly addressed. According to Puntland officials, the Mudug region has become a particular focus of concern, with reports of increased federal military activity fueling fears of further escalation. The Puntland government has vowed to take what it describes as appropriate measures to protect the region’s security and constitutional authority. The dispute marks the latest chapter in the deepening political rift between Puntland and the Federal Government, whose relations have deteriorated sharply over disagreements concerning constitutional reforms, electoral arrangements, federal-state powers, and governance. The meddling and interference of Villa Somalia to alter the balance of power inside Puntland without broad political consensus risks inflaming an already fragile relationship between Mogadishu and one of the country’s most influential federal member states. As accusations and counteraccusations continue to intensify, concerns are mounting that Somalia’s unresolved political disputes could further strain relations between the Federal Government and Puntland unless addressed through dialogue and constitutional mechanisms rather than confrontation. items.title: Muse Bihi Calls for Rethink of Somaliland-Israel Deal, Citing Rapidly Shifting Global Alliances
items.description: Hargeisa (WDN) – Former Somaliland President Muse Bihi Abdi has called on the Somaliland government to carefully reassess its diplomatic posture, warning that rapidly changing geopolitical dynamics in the Middle East could dramatically reshape alliances across the Horn of Africa and beyond. In a statement that has attracted significant political attention, Bihi urged the government to reconsider its understanding with Israel, arguing that the evolving international landscape demands strategic caution and foreign policy decisions firmly anchored in Somaliland’s long-term national interests. “Today, the world is facing profound political transformations and geopolitical turbulence,” Bihi said. “The conflict in the Middle East has already begun to cast its negative effects over the Horn of Africa.” The former president pointed to the ongoing diplomatic engagement between Iran and the United States, saying its outcome could fundamentally reshape the global political, security, and economic order, particularly in the Middle East and the Horn of Africa. According to Bihi, the growing influence of major Muslim powers including Iran, Pakistan, Türkiye, Egypt, and Saudi Arabia is becoming increasingly evident. He said the changing regional landscape could encourage closer cooperation among these countries. Bihi also suggested that emerging policy differences between the leaderships of the United States and Israel could become a significant factor in reshaping international alliances, with consequences that should not be underestimated. “It is becoming increasingly clear that the geopolitical landscape is changing,” he said. “These developments will have far-reaching implications that require careful analysis rather than hasty political decisions.” The former Somaliland leader urged the current administration to conduct a comprehensive assessment of the risks and opportunities arising from these global shifts before committing itself to long-term diplomatic arrangements. “It is essential that the government—particularly the Somaliland administration—carefully evaluate the potential consequences of these international developments to avoid strategic miscalculations that could undermine the nation’s interests,” he said. Bihi stressed that both past decisions and future foreign policy initiatives should be continuously reviewed and aligned with Somaliland’s national interests rather than short-term political considerations. His remarks have been widely interpreted as a call for strategic prudence at a time when the international order is undergoing significant realignment. Rather than viewing foreign policy through a static lens, Bihi argued that Somaliland must remain adaptable to an increasingly fluid geopolitical environment, where shifting alliances and regional power dynamics could redefine diplomatic priorities. The statement has reignited debate over Somaliland’s foreign policy direction, with many observers describing it as one of the clearest acknowledgments by a senior Somaliland political figure that developments far beyond the Horn of Africa could significantly influence the region’s diplomatic, economic, and security landscape in the years ahead. items.title: NISA Captures Fugitive Wanted by the FBI
items.description: Mogadishu (WDN) – In a major breakthrough for international law enforcement cooperation, Somalia’s National Intelligence and Security Agency (NISA) has arrested Abdikarim Eidleh, a fugitive accused by U.S. authorities of playing a central role in the multi-million-dollar Feeding Our Future fraud scandal—one of the largest COVID-19 relief fraud schemes in American history. The Office of the United States Attorney confirmed that Eidleh was apprehended in Mogadishu following a joint effort between the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) and Somalia’s National Intelligence and Security Agency (NISA), underscoring the growing security cooperation between the two countries. Abdikarim Eidleh Eidleh, 42, is accused of serving as a key associate of Aimee Bock, the founder of the nonprofit organization Feeding Our Future , which U.S. prosecutors allege orchestrated a massive scheme to defraud the federal government of hundreds of millions of dollars through programs intended to feed children during the COVID-19 pandemic. According to U.S. prosecutors, Eidleh helped establish a network of fraudulent companies and fictitious meal distribution sites, falsely claiming that thousands of children were being fed every day. Those fabricated claims allegedly enabled conspirators to obtain millions of dollars in federal reimbursements for meals that were never prepared or served. Investigators believe Eidleh fled the United States before the government’s investigation became public, spending years in hiding in Africa while American authorities continued their efforts to locate him. His capture marks a significant milestone in the long-running investigation. U.S. Attorney Daniel N. Rosen hailed the arrest as a clear demonstration that individuals accused of defrauding American taxpayers cannot evade justice by fleeing overseas. “Today’s arrest sends a powerful message,” Rosen said, “that those who steal from public programs and exploit vulnerable communities will be pursued wherever they attempt to hide.” The FBI also praised Somalia’s intelligence service for its decisive role in locating and apprehending the suspect, expressing appreciation to NISA for its close cooperation in bringing one of the case’s alleged key figures into custody. The arrest represents another example of Somalia’s increasing engagement in international law enforcement operations, as its security agencies expand cooperation with global partners in pursuing suspects linked to transnational crimes. For investigators, Eidleh’s capture is expected to strengthen one of the largest fraud prosecutions in recent U.S. history. For Somalia, it showcases NISA’s growing operational capability and its willingness to collaborate with international partners in bringing high-profile fugitives to justice. items.title: Key Feeding Our Future fraud suspect arrested in Somalia
items.description: Mogadishu, Somalia — A Minnesota man accused of helping run one of the largest pandemic-era fraud schemes in the United States has been taken into custody in Mogadishu, US prosecutors said, more than three years after he was indicted in the Feeding Our Future case. Abdikerm Abdelahi Eidleh, 42, of Burnsville, Minnesota, was arrested on June 25 in the Somali capital, the US Attorney’s Office for the District of Minnesota said Friday. Prosecutors described Eidleh as “one of the orchestrators” of the scheme, which they say stole hundreds of millions of dollars from a federal programme meant to feed children during the Covid-19 pandemic. The Justice Department said Eidleh was first charged in September 2022. He faces 31 counts, including conspiracy to commit wire fraud, wire fraud, federal programme bribery, money laundering conspiracy and money laundering. Court records showed Eidleh had not yet entered a plea and did not show whether he had appointed a lawyer. Arrest in Mogadishu US officials gave few details about how Somali authorities located and detained Eidleh or when he could appear before a court in Minnesota. But they credited the FBI and Somalia’s National Intelligence and Security Agency for helping track him down. “This defendant was a central figure in one of the largest fraud schemes in Minnesota history,” said Assistant Attorney General Colin M. McDonald of the Justice Department’s National Fraud Enforcement Division. “He not only stole taxpayer dollars, but he also robbed vulnerable children of critical resources they desperately needed,” McDonald said. “Rather than answer for his crimes in the United States, he fled to Somalia in a futile attempt to evade justice.” US Attorney Daniel N. Rosen said the arrest showed that suspects accused of stealing from government programmes could not evade prosecution by leaving the country. “Eidleh’s capture shows that, if you commit fraud against the American taxpayer and try hiding across the globe, the long arm of justice will find you,” Rosen said. FBI Minneapolis Special Agent in Charge Christopher D. Dotson said the arrest also showed the reach of US law enforcement partnerships. “The FBI’s partnerships with law enforcement worldwide again send a message – the FBI’s reach is far and wide, we will track down and bring to justice any fugitive, from anywhere,” Dotson said. “The FBI extends its sincere appreciation to the National Intelligence and Security Agency of Somalia for their outstanding partnership in locating and apprehending Eidleh so he may be brought to justice.” Pay-to-play claims Feeding Our Future was a Minnesota non-profit that sponsored meal sites under the Federal Child Nutrition Program, which expanded during the pandemic as Washington relaxed some rules to help feed children outside schools. Prosecutors say the organisation and its associates used the programme to enrol fraudulent meal sites across Minnesota, claiming they were feeding thousands of children every day, and then diverting federal reimbursements. The Justice Department said Feeding Our Future opened more than 250 sites and fraudulently obtained and disbursed more than $240 million in federal nutrition funds. Authorities say Eidleh worked for Feeding Our Future and helped recruit and support sites under its sponsorship. According to the indictment, Eidleh and other employees solicited and received bribes and kickbacks from individuals and companies seeking approval to operate fraudulent websites. Prosecutors say Feeding Our Future ran a “pay-to-play” system in which site operators kicked back part of their proceeds to employees, including Eidleh, often disguising the payments as “consulting fees” through shell companies. The indictment also alleges that Eidleh created his own child nutrition sites using nominee owners, falsely claimed they served meals to thousands of children a day, and created shell companies that appeared to sell food to those sites. He then submitted fraudulent invoices and deposited more than $5 million in kickbacks, bribes and other proceeds into accounts linked to his shell companies, prosecutors said. Wider prosecution The arrest comes one month after Aimee Bock, the founder and executive director of Feeding Our Future, was sentenced to 500 months in prison — more than 41 years — for her lead role in the scheme. Bock was convicted at trial alongside Salim Said, a former co-owner of Safari Restaurant. Prosecutors said the two oversaw a network of meal sites that falsely claimed to have served millions of meals. “Over forty-one years in prison is the cost this fraudster will pay for stealing from children,” McDonald said after Bock’s sentencing. The Feeding Our Future investigation has become one of the largest fraud prosecutions in Minnesota history. By March, prosecutors said they had secured 63 convictions across the wider case, calling it the largest number of convictions in a single fraud investigation by the Minnesota US Attorney’s Office in recent memory. The Justice Department has said 78 defendants have been charged in the broader Feeding Our Future investigation, which it described as the largest COVID-19 fraud scheme in the country. Fraud crackdown Federal investigators have kept the case as a priority as Washington intensifies action against pandemic-era fraud and alleged abuse of benefit programmes. The Justice Department said the FBI, IRS Criminal Investigation, the US Postal Inspection Service and Homeland Security Investigations investigated the case. FBI Minneapolis Special Agent in Charge Christopher D. Dotson said the detention in Somalia showed the reach of US law enforcement partnerships. “The FBI’s reach is far and wide,” Dotson said. “We will track down and bring to justice any fugitive, from anywhere.” He said Eidleh’s alleged fraud “took millions of dollars from programs designed for children and families in need”. The indictment remains an allegation, and Eidleh is presumed innocent unless proven guilty in court. items.title: Macawiisleyda Hiiraan oo war kasoo saaray hanjabaaddii FIQI
items.description: Beledweyne (Caasimada Online) – Macawiisleyda Beesha Xawaadle ee gobolka Hiiraan ayaa si kulul uga hadlay hadalka soo yeeray Wasiirka Gaashaandhigga, Axmed Macallin Fiqi oo maanta weerar afka ah ku qaaday Agaasimihii hore ee NISA, Cabdullahi Sanbaloolshe oo kasoo jeedo gobolkaasi. Fiqi oo maanta Beledweyne uga qayb-galay xuska maalinta xorriyadda ee dalka Jabuuti ayaa sheegay in Sanbaloolshe iyo nimanka kale ee mucaaradka ee dhawaan magaalada Muqdisho kula dagaalamay dowladda ay doonayeen in la gubo caasimada, balse isku daygoodii laga hortegay, sida uu ku dooday. Sidoo kale wuxuu tilmaamay in nimanka sidaas sameeyay la fasaxay, isla markaana ay weli sii doodayaan, sida in dhib loo gaystay oo kale. “Ninka madfaca kusoo riday Madaxtooyada Soomaaliya ayaa wuxuu leeyahay waa lay soo weeraray ninka haamaha shidaalka dekedda rabay inuu gubo oo 10 mitir u jirsaday hoobihii uu riday haamaha magaalada oo dhan gubi lahaa ayaa wuxuu leeyahay waa lay dili rabay weligey ma cafinayo inuu noolyahay ayaa naxariis ah oo weliba la fasaxay,” ayuu yiri Wasiir Axmed Macallin Fiqi. Intaas kadib waxaa soo jawaabay Macawiisleyda Hiiraan oo sheegay inay garab taagan yihiin Sanbaloolshe, waxayna wax laga xumaado ku tilmaamay hadalka kasoo yeeray Wasiirka Gaashaandhigga Xukuumadda Soomaaliya. “Sanbaloolshe lama dili karo cidina uma gefi karto waa Libaax ina sankataabte ayaa la yiraahdaa haddii uu Fiqi Habargidir yahay, Sanbaloolshana waa nimanka la yiraahdo Xawaadle.” ayuu yiri sarkaal u hadlay Macawiisleyda. Sidoo kale wuxuu intaas ku daray in ay diyaar u yihiin inay difaacaan Sanbaloolshe, haddii la’isku dayo in khatar la geliyo nafsaddiisa. “Sanbaloolshe kaligiis ma’aha ciidankiisa ayaana diyaar u ah haddii aan nahay Macawiisleyd waa kacsanahay waxayna diidan yihiin gardarrada,” ayuu sii raaciyay. Si kastaba, Hadalkan ayaa daba socda is weerarka dhanka baraha bulshada ee muxaafadka iyo mucaaradka oo dhawaan dagaal toos ah uu ku dhex-mara xaafado ka tirsan magaalada Muqdisho, kaas oo gaystay khasaare kala duwan. items.title: Ururka JSP oo  ansixiyey murashaxnimada Liibaan Axmed Xasan ee xilka Hoggaamiyaha Galmudug
items.description: Xarunta Dhexe ee Ururka Caddaaladda iyo Wadajirka (JSP) ayaa maanta lagu qabtay kulanka Guddiga Fulinta ee ururka, kaas oo uu shir-guddoominayay Xoghayaha Guud ee ururka, Dr. Xuseen Sheekh Maxamuud. Kulanka ayaa diiradda lagu saaray u diyaar-garowga doorashada soo socota ee Dowlad Goboleedka Galmudug iyo qorsheyaasha ururka ee ku aaddan ka qeybgalka doorashada. Kadib dood iyo falanqeyn, Guddiga Fulinta ee Ururka Caddaaladda iyo Wadajirka (JSP) ayaa si aqlabiyad leh u ansixiyay in Mudane Liibaan Axmed Xasan uu noqdo musharraxa rasmiga ah ee ururka u metelaya doorashada Madaxweynaha Dowlad Goboleedka Galmudug ee muddo-xileedka 2026–2031. Ururka JSP ayaa sheegay in magacaabistani ay ka tarjumeyso kalsoonida uu ku qabo hoggaanka iyo kartida Liibaan Axmed Xasan, iyadoo la xusay in maalmaha soo socda la dardargelin doono ololaha iyo diyaar-garowga doorashada Galmudug.

Kadib dood iyo falanqeyn, Guddiga Fulinta ee Ururka Caddaaladda iyo Wadajirka (JSP) ayaa si aqlabiyad leh u ansixiyay in Mudane Liibaan Axmed Xasan uu noqdo musharraxa rasmiga ah ee ururka u metelaya doorashada Madaxweynaha Dowlad Goboleedka Galmudug ee muddo-xileedka 2026–2031. Ururka JSP ayaa sheegay in magacaabistani ay ka tarjumeyso kalsoonida uu ku qabo hoggaanka iyo kartida Liibaan Axmed Xasan, iyadoo la xusay in maalmaha soo socda la dardargelin doono ololaha iyo diyaar-garowga doorashada Galmudug.

Daawo: Fiqi oo kasoo duulay Beledweyne iyo Sanbaloolshe oo…
items.description: Muqdisho (Caasimada Online) – Wasiirka Gaashaandhigga Soomaaliya, Axmed Macallin Fiqi oo saaka booqasho ku tegay magaalada Beledweyne oo uu uga qayb-galay maalinta xorriyadda ee dalka Jamhuuriyadda Jabuuti ayaa galabta dib ugu soo laabtay magaalada Muqdisho ee caasimada dalka. Fiqi oo intii uu ku sugnaa Beledweyne weeraray Agaasimihii hore ee NISA, Cabdullahi Maxamed Cali (Sanbaloolshe) iyo xubnaha kale ee mucaaradka ayaa sheegay in naxariis ay tahay haddii ay maanta noolyihiin, kadib dagaalkii ay dhawaan magaaada Muqdisho kula galeen ciidamada dowladda Soomaaliya. Intaas kadib hadalka wasiirka ayaa dhaliyay caro xooggan, waxaana soo baxday warar sheegaya in Macawiiseyda Hiiraan ay is abaabuleen, iyaga ka xumaaday hadalkaas, isla markaana si weyn loogu baahiyay baraha bulshada in uu socda qorshe ay ku hor istaagayaan in Fiqi uu ka baxo magaaladaasi. Hase’ahaatee, Wasiirka oo ay wehliyaan mas’uuliyiinta maamulka degmada iyo madax sare oo ka tirsan HirShabelle ayaa ugu dambeyn si nabad uga soo kicitimay halkaasi, kadibna dib ugu soo laabtay magaalada Muqdisho. Axmed Macallin Fiqi oo ka hadlay wararka baahay ayaa beeniyay, wuxuuna tilmaamay in Beledweyne ay tahay magaaladiisa, uuna ka shaqeynayo hormarkeda. “Waxa igu hareereysan waa Xawaadle, HirShabelle oo dhan ayaa ila socota si nabad ah ayaana ku duuleynaa,” ayuu yiri Wasiirka Gaashaandhigga Sidoo kale wuxuu sii raaciyay “Magaaladan waa magaaladaydii waxaasna waa hadallo raqiis ah magaaladan sidii ay ku hormari lahayd, dalkaana ku hormari lahaa baan ka shaqeyneynaa”. Dhinaca kale, waxaa mar kale soo hadlay Cabdullahi Sanbaloolshe oo jawaab siiyay Wasiirka Gaashaandhigga, isaga oo tilmaamay in hadalkiisa uu caddeyn u yahay in Madaxweyne Xasan Sheekh iyo kooxdiisa ay bannaysteen dhiigooda”. “Cabsi ma jebiso dad horay u bartay adkeysi Hadalka ay ka muuqato fulaynimadu ee Axmed Macallin Fiqi oo ah in nala dilo aniga, madaxda kale iyo duubabkii dhaqanka ee nagula weeraray xaafadda Barmuudo 3-4 bisha june, si naloo qaarajiyo, balse uu ku tilmaamay in ay “naxariis” tahay in aan weli nool nahay oo ay ahayd in nala dilo.” ayuu yiri Agaasimihii hore ee NISA. “Hadalka Wasiirka Gaashaandhigga Xukuumadda xil-gaarsiinta, waxa uu caddayn u yahay in Xasan Sheekh iyo kooxdiisa ay bannaysteen dhiigeenna, si ay noo cabsi-geliyaan oo ay xukunka sharci-darro kusii joogaan. Marnaba nalagu cabsi-gelin kari maayo. Waxaannu hore u soo marnay oo uga adkaanay rajiimyo ka adag kan. “Qofka bartay sida loo dhinto, wuxuu illoobay sida addoon loo noqdo.” Cabsi ma jebiso dad hore u bartay adkaysiga”.   The post Daawo: Fiqi oo kasoo duulay Beledweyne iyo Sanbaloolshe oo… appeared first on Caasimada Online .

items.title: Kenya deports Somalia deputy prime minister over alleged passport irregularities
items.description: Kenya has deported Somalia’s Second Deputy Prime Minister, Jibril Abdirashid Haji, after immigration officials accused him of holding a Kenyan passport that authorities believe may have been obtained fraudulently, according to a Kenyan police report.

items.title: EU tightens visa rules for Somalis over returns row
items.description: Brussels, Belgium — The European Union on Thursday tightened visa rules for Somali nationals, saying Mogadishu has failed to cooperate sufficiently in taking back citizens who have no legal right to remain in Europe. The Council of the European Union said the temporary measures followed an assessment by the European Commission, which found Somalia’s cooperation on readmission “insufficient”. The decision means EU member states can no longer issue multiple-entry visas to Somali nationals, waive documentary requirements for applicants, or waive visa fees for holders of Somali diplomatic and service passports. The standard processing period for visa applications will also rise to 45 calendar days from 15. “The objective is to encourage Somalia to improve cooperation on readmission,” the Council said, adding that the European Commission would continue to assess any progress. The suspension has no fixed end date. Somali President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud rejected the EU’s accusation, saying Mogadishu had not refused to receive its citizens but wanted European governments to verify that people marked for return were genuinely Somali. “We have not rejected our people. Our people belong to this country, and we cannot reject them,” Hassan Sheikh said. No visa ban The measures do not amount to a visa ban on Somali travellers. But they will make the process slower, stricter and more costly for applicants seeking short stays in the Schengen area for family visits, business, study, medical treatment or official travel. A Schengen short-stay visa generally allows non-EU nationals to remain in the bloc for up to 90 days in any 180-day period. The decision follows months of pressure from EU governments, which have been seeking to increase returns of rejected asylum seekers and other migrants staying irregularly in the bloc. EU home affairs ministers discussed Somalia earlier this month at a meeting in Luxembourg, where officials said irregular arrivals of Somali nationals had more than doubled between 2024 and 2025, with many journeys facilitated by smuggling networks. Cyprus deputy migration minister Nicholas Ioannides said after the talks that EU governments had agreed to use “all available tools” when countries refused to cooperate on returns. “We need to make use of all the tools at our disposal, including restrictive visa measures, when a third country insists on not being responsive regarding return and readmission,” Ioannides said. Return pressure The Commission first proposed the restrictions in 2024 under Article 25a of the EU Visa Code, a mechanism that allows the bloc to use visa policy as leverage when non-EU countries do not cooperate on readmission. In that proposal, the Commission said Somalia’s return rate stood at just 4 per cent in 2023, citing problems with identifying Somali nationals, issuing emergency travel documents, and organising return operations. EU officials also said member states faced “persistent challenges” because Somalia had not provided clear interlocutors and had given limited responses to readmission requests, particularly in cases involving forced returns. The Commission said the measures were proportionate and would not stop Somalis from applying for visas or receiving them. It also pointed to practical difficulties in processing Somali visa applications, including the absence of any EU member state present or represented in Somalia to issue visas, and differences among European governments over the recognition of Somali travel documents. Somali nationals lodged 1,600 Schengen visa applications in 2022 and 2,600 in 2023, with around 1,000 and 1,600 visas issued respectively, according to the Commission’s 2024 proposal. Identity checks Hassan Sheikh said Somalia’s dispute with the EU centred on verification, not a refusal to take back Somali citizens. He said some people from the wider Horn of Africa had claimed Somali identity in Europe to seek asylum, making it necessary for Mogadishu to confirm nationality before accepting returns. “The only question we have is about the way these people are being returned,” he said. “Everyone from the Horn of Africa who has our colour and appearance has claimed our name in order to get political asylum.” He said Somalia had previously received people described as Somali who did not speak Somali and were not Somali nationals. “Today, our position is this: let us verify whether these people are citizens of the Federal Republic of Somalia. That is the only issue between us,” he said. Somalia has previously pushed back against forced deportations while saying it welcomes the voluntary return of its citizens. During a visit to Berlin in November 2024, President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud told German Chancellor Olaf Scholz there was no need for forced repatriation of Somalis living in Germany, according to comments relayed by the Somali presidency. “They are welcome back to their homeland, reunite with their families, and reintegrate into their communities, where they can contribute to the country’s development and be part of Somalia’s collective progress,” Mohamud said. Uneasy partnership The latest EU move comes despite recent efforts to maintain a broader partnership with Somalia. In May, the EU and the Somali federal government held their first Partnership Dialogue under the Samoa Agreement in Mogadishu, pledging to strengthen cooperation on peace and security, governance, justice, migration and economic development. The two sides also agreed to continue technical discussions on returns and readmission. But Thursday’s decision signals growing impatience in Brussels, where migration remains one of Europe’s most politically sensitive issues. The EU’s new Pact on Migration and Asylum entered into application this month, promising faster asylum procedures, stronger border controls, greater burden-sharing between member states and closer cooperation with countries of origin and transit. Eurostat figures show first-time asylum applications in EU countries fell by 27 per cent in 2025, to 669,400, but Somali nationals remained among notable groups in the system. Somalis received 13,665 protection statuses in the EU last year, accounting for 3.8 per cent of all people granted protection. Somalia was also among the top countries of origin for unaccompanied minors seeking asylum, with 2,290 applications in 2025. At the same time, EU governments have sought to raise the number of people returned after being ordered to leave. In the fourth quarter of 2025, 117,545 non-EU citizens received orders to leave an EU country, while 33,860 returned to third countries. For Somalia, the visa decision adds a new point of friction with a major donor and security partner at a time when Mogadishu continues to seek European support for state-building, counter-terrorism, development and humanitarian needs. items.title: US and Somali authorities arrest suspect in Minnesota pandemic fraud case
items.description: Mogadishu, Somalia — United States prosecutors have arrested a man in Somalia accused of playing a leading role in one of the largest pandemic-related fraud cases in US history.

items.title: Ingiriiska oo qorshe cusub u samaynaya qaxootiga doonaya in galaan dalkiisa
items.description: Wasaaradda arrimaha gudaha ee UK ayaa sheegtay in ay qorsheynayaan in ay soo bandhigaan wadooyin cusub oo “ammaan ah oo sharci ah” oo ay qaxootiga ku soo galaan dalka sanadkan. Wasaaraddu waxay ku dhawaaqday inay u oggolaan doonto hay’adaha sida jaamacadaha, kooxaha bulshada iyo ganacsiyada inay taageeraan qaxootiga soo codsaday inay yimaadaan UK, iyadoo loo eegayo qaab la mid ah nidaamka qaxootiga ee Canada. Balse xisbiga Conservative-ka ee Britain ayaa ka jawaabay oo sheegay in dadka magangelyodoonka ah aan loo ogolaan karin dalka ilaa laga joojinayo socdaalka sharci darrada ah. Xoghayaha arrimaha gudaha ee Britain Shabana Mahmood ayaa sheegtay in nidaamka cusub uu ilaalin doono “qaxootiga dhabta ah” iyadoo la xirayo “kanaalada xadgudubka ah”. “Britain waxay had iyo jeer magangalyo siin jirtay kuwa ka soo cararaya dagaalka iyo cadaadiska. Laakiin nidaamka wuxuu noolaan karaa oo keliya haddii dadku ku kalsoonaadaan inuu yahay mid caddaalad ah, la xakameyn karo oo aan lagu xadgudbin,” ayay tiri. Ms Mahmood waxa ay isku dayaysaa in ay taageero u dhisto sharcigeeda socdaalka ka hor inta aanu Andy Burnham noqon raysal wasaare. Sharcigan ayaa lagu wadaa in todobaadkan la horgeeyo aqalka baarlamaanka, iyadoo la filayo in qaar ka mid ah xildhibaanada shaqaalaha ay ka soo horjeestaan ​​qaar ka mid ah qodobadiisa. Shabana Mahmud, oo ay dhiirigelisay Denmark, ayaa horaantii sanadkan ku soo bandhigtay isbedelo waaweyn oo ku saabsan nidaamka magangalyada UK, oo ay ku jiraan in la siiyo magangalyo ku meel gaar ah qaxootiga iyo laba jibaar muddada ay tahay in muhaajiriintu ay sugaan si ay u helaan deganaansho rasmi ah. Isbeddellada ayaa ka cadhaysiiyay qaar ka mid ah xubnaha Labour-ka oo dareemaya in la heli karo ammaan badan, waddooyin sharci ah oo lagu tago UK si ay uga niyad jabaan doomaha yar yar inay gudbaan. Qorshahan cusub ee lagu dhawaaqay habeenimadii Jimcaha, ayaa waxaa dhiirigeliyay barnaamijka ilaalinta bulshada ee Canada, kaasoo si guul leh dib u dejin ugu sameeyay ku dhawaad ​​400,000 oo qaxooti ah tan iyo markii la bilaabay 1979-kii. Xafiiska arrimaha gudaha ee UK ayaa sheegay in Kanada, 70% qaxootiga la kafaalo-qaado ay shaqo helaan sanad gudihiis, taas oo 30% ka sarraysa kuwa dib-u-dejinta lagu sameeyay iyada oo loo marayo qorshayaasha dawladda. Boqortooyada Midowday (UK) waxay hadda haysataa tiro yar oo qaxoonti ah oo ay dhaqaale ku taageeraan kooxo kala duwan oo hoos yimaada Qorshaha Dib-u-dejinta UK, halka Home Office uu sheegay in “inta badan” qaxootiga ay taageeraan golayaasha deegaanka. Dowladda Britain ayaa cadaadis lagu saaray in la dhimo tirada dadka magangelyo doonka ah ee la dejiyo hoteelada iyadoo qarashka canshuur bixiyayaasha laga bixiyo. Dadka sida sharci darrada ah ku imaanaya doomaha yar yar ayaa sidoo kale wiiqay kalsoonida shacabka ee nidaamka magangalyada dalka. Dariiqyada cusubi waxay u oggolaanayaan tiro badan oo ururo ah, oo ay ku jiraan “jaamacado la aamini karo” iyo kooxaha bulshada sida kaniisadaha, inay taageeraan kuwa soo galaya. Hay’adahan ayaa mas’uul ka noqon doona taageerada qaxootiga si ay u helaan guri iyo shaqo. Si loo dhaqan geliyo qorshahan, dawladdu waxay kala shaqayn doontaa hay’adda Qaramada Midoobay u qaabilsan qaxootiga si loo go’aamiyo xaq u yeelashada magan-gelyo doonka, waxaana la hubin doonaa taariikhda soo jireenka ah ka hor intaysan soo gelin UK. Xafiiska Arrimaha Gudaha ee UK ayaa ku dhawaaqay in dariiqa shaqada qaxootiga la filayo inuu furmo sanadka soo socda, taasoo u ogolaanaysa loo-shaqeeyayaasha inay kafaala qaadaan qaxootiga. Codsiyada dariiqa jaamacadda ayaa lagu wadaa inay furmaan dabayaaqada sanadkan, iyadoo la qorsheeyay qaadashada ugu horreysa ee 2027. Dawladdu ma aysan sheegin tirada dadka loo ogolaanayo in ay maraan waddooyinkan cusub, balse waxay sheegtay in la xadidi doono oo lagu bilaabi doono tiro yar. Sidoo kale waxaa la sheegay in Wasaaradda Arrimaha Gudaha ay koontarooli doonto Hay’adaha kaalmeyn kara dhaqaalaha, isla markaana cid kasta oo soo codsata la marsiin doono baaritaan adag. Chris Phillip, xoghayaha arrimaha gudaha hadhka konserfatifka, ayaa sheegay in ilaa socdaalka sharci darada ahi eber ka noqonayo, “waa inaanan dad kale u ogolaanin ‘sababo bini’aadantinimo’.” Wuxuu ku eedeeyay xisbiga shaqaalaha inay taageerayaan “xuduudaha furan” wuxuuna sheegay in tillaabooyinka “aysan joojin doonin socdaalka sharci darrada ah.” Sidoo kale furitaanka wadooyin cusub oo soo gala UK ee qaxootiga, Xafiiska Arrimaha Gudaha waxa uu ku dhawaaqay in uu wax ka qaban doono sheegashooyinka magangelyo ee been abuurka ah Bbc somali

Ms Mahmood waxa ay isku dayaysaa in ay taageero u dhisto sharcigeeda socdaalka ka hor inta aanu Andy Burnham noqon raysal wasaare. Sharcigan ayaa lagu wadaa in todobaadkan la horgeeyo aqalka baarlamaanka, iyadoo la filayo in qaar ka mid ah xildhibaanada shaqaalaha ay ka soo horjeestaan ​​qaar ka mid ah qodobadiisa. Shabana Mahmud, oo ay dhiirigelisay Denmark, ayaa horaantii sanadkan ku soo bandhigtay isbedelo waaweyn oo ku saabsan nidaamka magangalyada UK, oo ay ku jiraan in la siiyo magangalyo ku meel gaar ah qaxootiga iyo laba jibaar muddada ay tahay in muhaajiriintu ay sugaan si ay u helaan deganaansho rasmi ah. Isbeddellada ayaa ka cadhaysiiyay qaar ka mid ah xubnaha Labour-ka oo dareemaya in la heli karo ammaan badan, waddooyin sharci ah oo lagu tago UK si ay uga niyad jabaan doomaha yar yar inay gudbaan. Qorshahan cusub ee lagu dhawaaqay habeenimadii Jimcaha, ayaa waxaa dhiirigeliyay barnaamijka ilaalinta bulshada ee Canada, kaasoo si guul leh dib u dejin ugu sameeyay ku dhawaad ​​400,000 oo qaxooti ah tan iyo markii la bilaabay 1979-kii. Xafiiska arrimaha gudaha ee UK ayaa sheegay in Kanada, 70% qaxootiga la kafaalo-qaado ay shaqo helaan sanad gudihiis, taas oo 30% ka sarraysa kuwa dib-u-dejinta lagu sameeyay iyada oo loo marayo qorshayaasha dawladda. Boqortooyada Midowday (UK) waxay hadda haysataa tiro yar oo qaxoonti ah oo ay dhaqaale ku taageeraan kooxo kala duwan oo hoos yimaada Qorshaha Dib-u-dejinta UK, halka Home Office uu sheegay in “inta badan” qaxootiga ay taageeraan golayaasha deegaanka. Dowladda Britain ayaa cadaadis lagu saaray in la dhimo tirada dadka magangelyo doonka ah ee la dejiyo hoteelada iyadoo qarashka canshuur bixiyayaasha laga bixiyo. Dadka sida sharci darrada ah ku imaanaya doomaha yar yar ayaa sidoo kale wiiqay kalsoonida shacabka ee nidaamka magangalyada dalka. Dariiqyada cusubi waxay u oggolaanayaan tiro badan oo ururo ah, oo ay ku jiraan “jaamacado la aamini karo” iyo kooxaha bulshada sida kaniisadaha, inay taageeraan kuwa soo galaya. Hay’adahan ayaa mas’uul ka noqon doona taageerada qaxootiga si ay u helaan guri iyo shaqo. Si loo dhaqan geliyo qorshahan, dawladdu waxay kala shaqayn doontaa hay’adda Qaramada Midoobay u qaabilsan qaxootiga si loo go’aamiyo xaq u yeelashada magan-gelyo doonka, waxaana la hubin doonaa taariikhda soo jireenka ah ka hor intaysan soo gelin UK. Xafiiska Arrimaha Gudaha ee UK ayaa ku dhawaaqay in dariiqa shaqada qaxootiga la filayo inuu furmo sanadka soo socda, taasoo u ogolaanaysa loo-shaqeeyayaasha inay kafaala qaadaan qaxootiga. Codsiyada dariiqa jaamacadda ayaa lagu wadaa inay furmaan dabayaaqada sanadkan, iyadoo la qorsheeyay qaadashada ugu horreysa ee 2027. Dawladdu ma aysan sheegin tirada dadka loo ogolaanayo in ay maraan waddooyinkan cusub, balse waxay sheegtay in la xadidi doono oo lagu bilaabi doono tiro yar. Sidoo kale waxaa la sheegay in Wasaaradda Arrimaha Gudaha ay koontarooli doonto Hay’adaha kaalmeyn kara dhaqaalaha, isla markaana cid kasta oo soo codsata la marsiin doono baaritaan adag. Chris Phillip, xoghayaha arrimaha gudaha hadhka konserfatifka, ayaa sheegay in ilaa socdaalka sharci darada ahi eber ka noqonayo, “waa inaanan dad kale u ogolaanin ‘sababo bini’aadantinimo’.” Wuxuu ku eedeeyay xisbiga shaqaalaha inay taageerayaan “xuduudaha furan” wuxuuna sheegay in tillaabooyinka “aysan joojin doonin socdaalka sharci darrada ah.” Sidoo kale furitaanka wadooyin cusub oo soo gala UK ee qaxootiga, Xafiiska Arrimaha Gudaha waxa uu ku dhawaaqay in uu wax ka qaban doono sheegashooyinka magangelyo ee been abuurka ah Bbc somali

items.title: Eastern Libya bans Somalis, other nationalities from entry
items.description: Benghazi, Libya — Libya’s eastern-based government has banned nationals of Somalia, Sudan, Eritrea and Ethiopia from entering territory under its control, as authorities across the divided North African country intensify restrictions on migrants and refugees. The decree, issued Tuesday by the parallel administration in Benghazi, bars citizens of the four African countries from entering Libya through “all land, sea and air ports”. A source in the eastern administration told Reuters that the move aimed to “reorganise foreign nationals’ entry” into Libya. The government is headed by Osama Hamad and aligned with military commander Khalifa Haftar, whose forces control eastern Libya and large parts of the south. It operates separately from the internationally recognised government of Prime Minister Abdulhamid Dbeibah, based in Tripoli, which came to power through a UN-backed process in 2021. The decree exempts members of accredited diplomatic and consular missions and their families. It also allows workers in education, medicine and allied health professions to enter, provided they obtain official approvals and valid work contracts. Migrant route Somalis have for years used Libya as one of the main North African transit routes towards Europe, often crossing through Ethiopia, Sudan or the Sahara before attempting the dangerous Mediterranean journey. Libya has also long served as a destination and transit country for Sudanese, Eritreans and Ethiopians fleeing conflict, repression or poverty and seeking work or passage to Europe by sea. The decision comes as Sudan’s war, which erupted in April 2023, continues to drive large numbers of people across borders. The UN refugee agency estimated in March that more than 559,000 Sudanese refugees had fled to Libya since the start of the conflict between Sudan’s army and the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces. Many entered through the remote southeast, including the Kufra region, after crossing dangerous desert routes via Chad. The International Organisation for Migration said in its latest Libya migrant report that more than 936,000 migrants were present in the country in January and February, with Sudanese nationals making up the largest share. Crackdown The entry ban comes as rights groups warn of an escalating campaign against migrants by rival Libyan authorities. Amnesty International said Tuesday that both the Tripoli-based government and authorities in the east had carried out mass arrests , arbitrary detentions and collective expulsions over the past month. “It is abhorrent that rival Libyan authorities are uniting in the abuse of migrants and refugees,” said Diana Eltahawy, Amnesty’s deputy regional director for the Middle East and North Africa. The rights group said official rhetoric had fuelled anti-migrant protests, vigilantism and online hate speech. Earlier this month, hundreds of Libyans blocked the UN refugee agency’s office in Tripoli, chanting slogans against the settlement of migrants in the country. The latest restrictions also follow several deadly incidents on Libya’s migration routes. At least 15 migrant bodies, including that of a girl, washed ashore along Libya’s eastern Mediterranean coast last week after a boat believed to be carrying dozens of people capsized near Tobruk. In February, a UN human rights report said migrants in Libya faced killings, torture, rape, forced labour and arbitrary detention. One Eritrean woman held in a trafficking house in Tobruk told investigators: “I wish I died. It was a journey of hell.” Libya plunged into years of instability after a NATO-backed uprising toppled longtime ruler Muammar Gaddafi in 2011. Since 2014, the country has been split between rival authorities in the east and west, while armed groups, traffickers and security forces compete for control of lucrative migration routes. European governments have sought cooperation with Libyan authorities to reduce departures across the Mediterranean, but rights groups say such policies have trapped vulnerable people in a country where they face systematic abuse. items.title: EU Imposes Temporary Schengen Visa Restrictions on Somali Citizens
items.description: The European Union has introduced temporary restrictions on Schengen visa applications for Somali citizens, citing what it described as insufficient cooperation by Somalia in accepting the return of nationals ordered to leave EU member states.

items.title: Somalia says airstrikes kill at least 30 Al-Shabaab militants in Middle Shabelle
items.description: Somalia’s government says at least 30 Al-Shabaab militants were killed in a series of airstrikes carried out by the Somali National Armed Forces (SNAF), with support from international partners, in the Middle Shabelle region this week.

items.title: Tirada dhimashada dhulgariirka Venezula oo gaartay 920
items.description: Caracas ( Raxanreeb Online) In ka badan 900 oo qof ayaa la xaqiijiyay in ay ku dhinteen 3,360 kalena ay ku dhaawacmeen dhul gariir ka dhacay dalka Venezuela, sida ay sheegtay dowladda, iyadoo samatabbixiyeyaashu ay wadaan baadigoobka dad badbaaday. Dadka dhaawacmay ayaa lagu daweynayaa goobo caafimaad oo macmal ah, kaddib markii tobaneeyo dhismo oo ku yaalla waqooyiga dalkaas ay waxyeello kasoo gaartay labadii dhul-gariir oo ay ku jirto caasimadda Caracas. Sarkaal sare oo ka tirsan dowladda ayaa sheegay in boqollaal samatabbixiyaal caalami ah ay dalka soo gaareen, qaar kalena ay jidka ku soo jiraan. Laba dhul gariir oo xoog badan ayaa ku dhuftay Venezuela ilbiriqsiyo gudahood midba midka kale Arbacadii. Dhulgariirkii labaad oo cabirkiisa lagu qiyaasay 7.5 ayaa ahaa midkii ugu xooganaa ee dalkaasi ku dhuftay muddo qarni ah. Aagga La Guaira, oo ku yaalla waqooyiga caasimadda Caracas, ayaa ah meelaha ugu daran, sida ay saraakiishu sheegeen. Dad badan ayaa weli la la’yahay, iyadoo saraakiisha ay ka cabsi qabaan in dhimashadu ay kororto xitaa iyadoo ay socdaan gurmadka. items.title: Maxaa ka jira in Lafta-gareen uu dib u heshiisin la bilaabay DF?
items.description: Nairobi (Caasimada Online) – Madaxweynihii hore ee Koonfur Galbeed Soomaaliya, welina ku doodayo inuu yahay Madaxweynaha sharciga ah oo qoraal soo saaray ayaa ka hadlay warar lagu baahiyay baraha bulshada oo sheegayay inuu dib u heshiisiin la bilaabay Dowladda Federaalka Soomaaliya, si loo soo afjaro dhaq-dhaqaaqyada ay weli ciidamadiisa ka wadaan aaga Baydhaba. Cabdicasiis Xasan Maxamed (Lafta-gareen) oo haatan ah dibad-joog ayaa beeniyay weerarkaasi, wuxuuna sheegay in aanu jiri qorshe dib u heshiisiineed oo la filanayo, sida uu ku caddeeyay warsaxaafadeedkiisa. Sidoo kale, wuxuu baaq u diray shacabka Koonfur Galbeed oo uu ka dalbaday in xogta saxda ah ee kala socdaan ilaha rasmiga ah, gaar ahaa xafiiskiisa iyo hay’adaha dowladda. “Waxaan shacabka ugu baaqeynaa inay ka feejignaadaan wararka aan la hubin saxnimadooda, isla markaana ay ku kalsoonaadaan oo kaliya warka iyo ogeysiisyada rasmiga ah ee kasoo baxay xafiiska rasmiga ah ee Madaxweynaha iyo hay’adaha rasmiga ah ee ay khuseyso,” ayuu yiri Lafta-gareen. Waxaa kale oo uu warsaxaafadeedka kusii daray “Faafinta warar aan xaqiiqo ku salaysnayn waxay horseedi karaan jahwareer iyo marin habaabin bulshada dhexdeeda ah. Sidaas darteed, waxaan ku boorrinaynaa dhammaan dadka isticmaala baraha bulshada inay xaqiijitaan xog kasta kahor inta aasan faafinin”. Lafta-gareen oo sidoo kale soo hadal qaaday arrimaha ciidamada iyo dhaq-dhaqaaqyada ka socda duleedka Baydhaba ayaa sheegay in dhankooda ay sii wadi doonaan howlgallada, isla markaana uu jeedka uu yahay inay soo celiyaan nabadda Koonfur Galbeed, sida uu hadalka u dhigay. “Waxay Dowladda Koonfur Galbeed markale xaqiijinaysaa in ciidamada Booliska gaarka ay si wadi doonaan gudasha waajibaadkooda dastuuriga ah ee ilaalinta amniga iyo difaaca shacabka, sugidda xasilloonida iyo dib usoo celinta nabadda dhammaan deegaannada Dowladda Koonfur Galbeed,” ayaa mar kale yiri bayaanka uu soo saaray Cabdicasiis Lafta-gareen. Hadalkan ayaa kusoo aadayo, iyada oo dhawana isbeddel uu ka dhacay magaalada Baydhaba, kadib markii doorashada Koonfur Galbeed uu kusoo baxay Hoggaamiye Aadan Madoobe. items.title: Houthis warn over Israeli troop deployment to Somaliland
items.description: Sanaa, Yemen — A senior official in Yemen’s Houthi movement has warned that the group would treat any Israeli or US military presence in Somali waters as a “legitimate target”, after reports that Israel deployed forces to Somaliland following its recognition of the breakaway Somali region. Mohammed al-Farah, a member of Ansarullah’s political bureau, said the group viewed the Red Sea and Bab al-Mandab Strait as central to Yemen’s national security. “We regard the Red Sea and Bab el-Mandeb Strait as a very important strategic region,” Farah said in remarks reported Monday. “Any movement by the Zionist-American enemy there will be interpreted as an attempt to establish hostile influence, dominate vital waterways, and threaten the security of the entire region, including Saudi Arabia itself,” he added. The Houthis, who control Yemen’s capital Sanaa and much of the country’s north, have repeatedly targeted Israel and shipping they describe as Israeli-linked since the start of the Gaza war, turning the Bab al-Mandab into one of the world’s most volatile maritime chokepoints. The narrow waterway links the Red Sea to the Gulf of Aden and sits between Yemen, Djibouti and Eritrea. Any escalation there threatens a route used by commercial shipping, energy supplies and international naval forces. ‘Red line’ Farah said any Israeli presence in Somali territorial waters would directly threaten Yemen. “We in Yemen view such activities as a direct threat to Yemen’s national security and sovereignty,” he said. He added that Houthi leader Abdul-Malik al-Houthi had issued “a clear and stern warning” that the group would “deal forcefully” with any Israeli or American military presence in Somaliland. Farah said the group would treat any such deployment as a “red line” and a “legitimate target”. He also rejected the argument that foreign bases or military deployments were needed to secure the Red Sea, saying regional states, especially countries bordering the waterway, should take responsibility. “The Red Sea is not an open arena for foreign powers,” he said, accusing Israel and the United States of seeking to use the route for “Zionist, aggressive, and American agendas and schemes”. The warning followed a Middle East Eye report , cited by Somalia Today, that Israel sent around 50 soldiers to Somaliland after recognising the breakaway Somali region as an independent state in December. The report, citing a senior Somali government official, said Somali intelligence believed the soldiers arrived after Israel resumed its war with Iran in late February. The official claimed Israel selected soldiers of African heritage, “especially Ethiopians”, to avoid drawing attention. Israel’s military declined to comment directly on the allegation, saying it was “a matter for the political echelon”, according to the report. Israel’s Foreign Ministry later issued a blunt denial through several official accounts, saying: “FAKE NEWS.” Somaliland authorities have not publicly confirmed the alleged deployment. ‘Training, not bases’ Somaliland’s Defence Minister Mohamed Yusuf Ali has denied that Israel has established a military base in the territory, but confirmed Israeli security support. “There is no Israeli military presence or military bases in Somaliland,” he said. “But Israel is helping Somaliland… they are supporting to train some of our police and military.” The denial has not ended speculation about the military dimension of the new relationship. Israeli Defence Minister Israel Katz said during talks with Somaliland President Abdirahman Mohamed Abdullahi in Israel that the two sides had maintained quiet security ties for years. “For many years, we cooperated under the radar in a series of operations that will remain classified,” Katz said. At a Tel Aviv business forum, Abdullahi presented Somaliland as a strategic and commercial partner for Israel. “Somaliland is open for business, and Somaliland is ready for Israeli investment,” he said. Israel became the first country to formally recognise Somaliland on December 26, a move Hargeisa welcomed, but Mogadishu fiercely rejected. Somaliland declared independence from Somalia in 1991 as the Somali state collapsed into civil war. It has since built its own institutions and maintained relative stability, but has not secured broad international recognition. Somalia’s federal government says Somaliland remains an integral part of its sovereign territory and has described Israel’s recognition as unlawful interference and a direct assault on Somali unity. Berbera, Somaliland’s main port, sits on the Gulf of Aden near the approaches to the Bab al-Mandab, making it strategically valuable for foreign powers seeking influence over Red Sea routes. The Houthis this month announced a ban on Israeli maritime navigation in the Red Sea after renewed regional escalation, heightening fears that any Israeli foothold near Yemen could turn Somaliland and Somali waters into a new regional flashpoint. The warning followed a Middle East Eye report , cited by Somalia Today, that Israel sent around 50 soldiers to Somaliland after recognising the breakaway Somali region as an independent state in December. The report, citing a senior Somali government official, said Somali intelligence believed the soldiers arrived after Israel resumed its war with Iran in late February. The official claimed Israel selected soldiers of African heritage, “especially Ethiopians”, to avoid drawing attention. Israel’s military declined to comment directly on the allegation, saying it was “a matter for the political echelon”, according to the report. Israel’s Foreign Ministry later issued a blunt denial through several official accounts, saying: “FAKE NEWS.” Somaliland authorities have not publicly confirmed the alleged deployment. ‘Training, not bases’ Somaliland’s Defence Minister Mohamed Yusuf Ali has denied that Israel has established a military base in the territory, but confirmed Israeli security support. “There is no Israeli military presence or military bases in Somaliland,” he said. “But Israel is helping Somaliland… they are supporting to train some of our police and military.” The denial has not ended speculation about the military dimension of the new relationship. Israeli Defence Minister Israel Katz said during talks with Somaliland President Abdirahman Mohamed Abdullahi in Israel that the two sides had maintained quiet security ties for years. “For many years, we cooperated under the radar in a series of operations that will remain classified,” Katz said. At a Tel Aviv business forum, Abdullahi presented Somaliland as a strategic and commercial partner for Israel. “Somaliland is open for business, and Somaliland is ready for Israeli investment,” he said. Israel became the first country to formally recognise Somaliland on December 26, a move Hargeisa welcomed, but Mogadishu fiercely rejected. Somaliland declared independence from Somalia in 1991 as the Somali state collapsed into civil war. It has since built its own institutions and maintained relative stability, but has not secured broad international recognition. Somalia’s federal government says Somaliland remains an integral part of its sovereign territory and has described Israel’s recognition as unlawful interference and a direct assault on Somali unity. Berbera, Somaliland’s main port, sits on the Gulf of Aden near the approaches to the Bab al-Mandab, making it strategically valuable for foreign powers seeking influence over Red Sea routes. The Houthis this month announced a ban on Israeli maritime navigation in the Red Sea after renewed regional escalation, heightening fears that any Israeli foothold near Yemen could turn Somaliland and Somali waters into a new regional flashpoint. items.title: Somali state cuts ties with federal government
items.description: Somalia’s South West state has suspended all cooperation with the federal government in Mogadishu, accusing it of arming militias and attempting to remove regional president Abdiaziz Hassan Mohamed Laftagareen. The diplomatic rupture follows disputes over constitutional amendments pushed by Mogadishu. Following similar recent boycotts by Puntland, Jubbaland, and the long-breakaway Somaliland, Mogadishu’s actual governing authority is rapidly shrinking, leaving the central government increasingly isolated. This situation favors Al-Shabaab insurgents and local militias, providing them with operational breathing room as federal and regional security forces turn their political focus against each other. But for the average Somali citizen, the development has increased uncertainty over the country’s stability. Without credible dialogue, this cascading collapse of federal cooperation threatens to permanently balkanize Somalia, reversing decades of painstaking international state-building and security efforts. Reuters

items.title: Maxay dhigantahay in Aqoonyahanka Soomaaliyeed loo magacaabay xilka Kaaliyaha Xoghayaha Guud Qaramada Midoobay ee arrimaha bani’aadannimada?
items.description: Xoghayaha Guud ee Qaramada Midoobay, António Guterres, ayaa u magacaabay Mohamed Yahya xilka Kaaliyaha Xoghayaha Guud ee Arrimaha Bani’aadannimada iyo Ku-Xigeenka Isuduwaha Gargaarka Degdegga ah ee Xafiiska Qaramada Midoobay ee Isuduwidda Arrimaha Bani’aadannimada (OCHA). Magacaabistan ayaa Mohamed Yahya ka dhigaysa mid ka mid ah mas’uuliyiinta ugu sarreeya ee hoggaanka arrimaha bani’aadannimada ee Qaramada Midoobay, isaga oo door muhiim ah ka qaadan doona isku dubbaridka gurmadka degdegga ah iyo howlaha gargaarka ee ka socda dalalka ay saameeyeen colaadaha iyo musiibooyinka. Dowladda Federaalka Soomaaliya ayaa si diirran u soo dhaweysay magacaabistan, iyadoo ku tilmaantay guul qaran iyo aqoonsi muujinaya doorka sii kordhaya ee ay Soomaaliya ku leedahay hoggaanka hay’adaha caalamiga ah. Wasiiru Dowlaha Arrimaha Dibadda Soomaaliya, Cali Cumar, ayaa hambalyo u diray Mohamed Yahya, isaga oo sheegay in xilkan uu yahay mid uu mudnaa. “Waxaan hambalyo u dirayaa Mudane Mohamed Yahya magacaabistan muhiimka ah. “Soomaaliya waxay ku faanaysaa in mid ka mid ah muwaadiniinteeda loo doortay xil sare oo hoggaamineed oo Qaramada Midoobay ah. Waxaan u rajaynaynaa guul iyo inuu sii xoojiyo howlaha muhiimka ah ee OCHA ee taageerada dadka u baahan gargaarka adduunka oo dhan,” ayuu yiri Wasiiru Dowlaha Arrimaha Dibadda XFS. Magacaabistan ayaa noqanaysa tallaabo  muujinaysa kororka kalsoonida beesha caalamka ay ku qabto khubarada Soomaaliyeed, iyadoo Dowladda Federaalka ay muujisay rajo ah in waayo-aragnimada iyo hoggaaminta Mohamed Yahya ay door weyn ka qaadan doonaan horumarinta howlaha bani’aadannimada ee Qaramada Midoobay.

items.title: Madaxweynaha oo furay itixaanka shahaadiga ee dugsiyada sare iyo dhexe
items.description: 𝐌𝐚𝐝𝐚𝐱𝐰𝐞𝐲𝐧𝐚𝐡𝐚 𝐉𝐚𝐦𝐡𝐮𝐮𝐫𝐢𝐲𝐚𝐝𝐝𝐚 𝐒𝐨𝐦𝐚𝐥𝐢𝐥𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐨𝐨 𝐦𝐚𝐚𝐧𝐭𝐚 𝐬𝐢 𝐫𝐚𝐬𝐦𝐢 𝐚𝐡 𝐮 𝐟𝐮𝐫𝐚𝐲 𝐈𝐦𝐭𝐢𝐱𝐚𝐚𝐧𝐤𝐚 𝐒𝐡𝐚𝐡𝐚𝐚𝐝𝐢𝐠𝐚 𝐚𝐡 𝐞𝐞 𝐃𝐮𝐠𝐬𝐢𝐲𝐚𝐝𝐚 𝐃𝐡𝐞𝐱𝐞 𝐢𝐲𝐨 𝐃𝐮𝐠𝐬𝐢𝐲𝐚𝐝𝐚 𝐒𝐚𝐫𝐞 Madaxweynaha Jamhuuriyadda Somaliland, Mudane Cabdiraxmaan Maxamed Cabdillaahi (Cirro), ayaa maanta Dugsiga Sare ee Faarax Oomaar ee Caasimadda Hargeysa si rasmi ah uga furay bilowga Imtixaannada Shahaadiga ah ee Dugsiyada Dhexe iyo Dugsiyada Sare ee dalka Jamhuuriyadda Somaliland, kaas oo sannad kasta lagu qiimeeyo heerka aqooneed ee ardayda dalka, laguna xaqiijiyo hufnaanta iyo tayada nidaamka Waxbarashada Qaranka JSL. Waxa xusid mudan in sannadkan 2026-ka ay ardaydii ugu badnay (𝟒𝟐,𝟓𝟏𝟗) taariikhda Somaliland u fadhiisteen Imtixaannada Shahaadiga ah ee Dugsiyada Dhexe iyo kuwa Sare ee Jamhuuriyadda Somaliland. Madaxweynuhu waxa uu hambalyo iyo dhiirrigelinba u diray dhammaan ardayda maanta u fadhiisatay Imtixaannada Shahaadiga ah, isaga oo u rajeeyey guul iyo in ay ka gaadhaan natiijooyin wacan oo ka turjumaysa dedaalkoodii, kartidooda iyo aqoonta ay muddada dheer soo baranayeen. Ugu dambayn, Madaxweynaha Jamhuuriyadda Somaliland waxa uu u mahad naqay Wasaaradda Waxbarashada, Barbaarinta iyo Sayniska JSL, Xafiiska Imtixaannada Qaranka, Ciidamada Booliska JSL, Macallimiinta iyo dhammaan cid kasta oo ka qayb qaadatay diyaarinta, sugidda iyo qabsoomidda Imtixaannada Shahaadiga ah ee Qaranka Jamhuuriyadda Somaliland.

items.title: Puntland Security Tensions Deepen Amid Rising Political Dispute
items.description: Garow e — Security concerns have resurfaced in Garowe, the capital of Somalia’s Puntland state, following reports of renewed tensions and clashes involving forces affiliated with the Puntland administration. Religious leaders in Garowe have called for a united stance against any actors threatening Puntland’s security, stability and political existence. In a strongly worded appeal, the clerics urged authorities and the public to confront any efforts aimed at destabilising the region. The administration of President Said Abdullahi Deni has accused Somalia’s Federal Government of seeking to undermine Puntland’s state institutions. Puntland officials also alleged that federal authorities were involved in military mobilisation and the movement of weapons in parts of the region. Mudug region is among the areas where Puntland officials say federal-linked military activity has been reported. The Puntland administration has said it will take measures in response to what it describes as threats to its security and stability. The Federal Government of Somalia has not immediately responded to the allegations. The post Puntland Security Tensions Deepen Amid Rising Political Dispute appeared first on Raxanreeb Online .

items.title: Somalia and International Partners Carry Out Fresh Airstrikes on Al-Shabaab Positions
items.description: Mogadishu — The Federal Government of Somalia said its forces, with support from international partners, have conducted a series of airstrikes targeting Al-Shabaab positions in several areas of the Middle Shabelle region. In a statement, the government said the operations were carried out in Gayfo, Ruun Idiris and Cali Gaduud, areas it described as key locations used by Al-Shabaab for fighter mobilisation, training activities, and the storage of weapons, ammunition and military supplies. According to the statement, the first airstrike took place on June 24 in Gayfo, where Somali authorities said an Al-Shabaab mobilisation centre was destroyed. The government said militants and military equipment were present at the site when it was struck. On June 25, three consecutive airstrikes were reportedly carried out against an Al-Shabaab training facility in Ruun Idiris, where the group was allegedly preparing fighters for future operations. The government said another strike on the same day targeted armed Al-Shabaab militants in Cali Gaduud, who were allegedly preparing to launch attacks and carry out terrorist activities. Somali authorities did not provide further details on casualties or the full scale of damage caused by the strikes. Al-Shabaab has not immediately commented on the government’s claims. The post Somalia and International Partners Carry Out Fresh Airstrikes on Al-Shabaab Positions appeared first on Raxanreeb Online .

items.title: Daawo: Fiqi oo u jawaabay Sanbaloolshe: “In uu nool yahay ayaa naxariis ah”
items.description: Muqdisho (Caasimada Online) – Wasiirka Wasaaradda Gaashaandhigga Axmed Macallin Fiqi ayaa si kulul ugu jawaabay Agaasimihii hore ee Hay’adda Sirdoonka iyo Nabadsugidda Qaranka Cabdullahi Maxamed Cali (Sanbaloolshe) oo xalay weerar afka ah ku qaaday Madaxweyne Xasan Sheekh Maxamuud. Sanbaloolshe oo wareysi gaar ah siiyay Shabelle Tv ayaa weerarkii lagu qaaday isaga iyo Ra’iisul wasaarihii hore Xasan Cali Khayre ku eedeeyay inuu amray Madaxweynaha Soomaaliya, isla markaana la rabay in la dilo, sida uu hadaka u dhigay. Sidoo kale, wuxuu ku hanjabay in uu aarsan doono, isla markaana uusan cafin doonin weerarka lagu beegsaday, illaa inta laga bixinayo garowshiyo. “Wallaahi Bilalahi Tallaahi inaanan loo cafineynin 100-ka sano ee soo socda haddii aanan la’isaga garaabin oo aan laga Towbad keenin oo aanan laga heshiin aniga nimaan ahay weligey ma cafinaayo,” ayuu yiri Sanbaloolshe. Waxaa kale oo uu kusii daray “Wuxuu rabay in meesha nagula baaba’sho 100% isaga ayaa amarka baxshay taleefankana waa dansaday”. Intaas kadib waxaa soo jawaabay Wasiir Axmed Macallin Fiqi oo sheegay in Sanbaloolshe iyo nimanka kale ee mucaaradka ay doonayeen in la gubo Muqdisho, balse isku daygoodii laga hortegay, sida uu ku dooday. Wasiirka Gaashaandhigga ayaa sidoo kale xusay in nimanka sidaas sameeyay la fasaxay, isla markaana ay weli sii doodayaan, sida in dhib loo gaystay oo kale. “Ninka madfaca kusoo riday Madaxtooyada Soomaaliya ayaa wuxuu leeyahay waa lay soo weeraray ninka haamaha shidaalka dekedda rabay inuu gubo oo 10 mitir u jirsaday hoobihii uu riday haamaha magaalada oo dhan gubi lahaa ayaa wuxuu leeyahay waa lay dili rabay weligey ma cafinayo inuu noolyahay ayaa naxariis ah oo weliba la fasaxay,” ayuu yiri Wasiir Axmed Macallin Fiqi. Si kastaba, Hadalkan ayaa daba socda is weerarka dhanka baraha bulshada ee muxaafadka iyo mucaaradka oo dhawaan dagaal toos ah uu ku dhex-mara xaafado ka tirsan magaalada Muqdisho, kaas oo gaystay khasaare kala duwan. items.title: Wanted Suspect in $5M U.S. Nutrition Fraud Arrested in Mogadishu
items.description: Mogadishu — Somali security authorities have arrested Abdikarim Abdullahi Idle, 42, in Mogadishu, in connection with a major U.S. fraud investigation linked to the Feeding Our Future child nutrition program. According to the U.S. Department of Justice, Idle was arrested on June 25, 2026, after allegedly fleeing the United States to avoid prosecution. U.S. prosecutors accuse him of playing a central role in a large-scale fraud scheme involving federal child nutrition funds. The indictment alleges that Idle, who was involved in the program’s operations, accepted bribes and kickbacks in exchange for approving fraudulent meal sites. These sites allegedly submitted false claims stating that they were providing daily meals to thousands of children under the U.S. federal Child Nutrition Program. Prosecutors further allege that Idle established multiple companies and entities under different names to submit false claims and move fraud proceeds. The U.S. Department of Justice said more than $5 million in alleged proceeds were deposited into bank accounts linked to companies associated with him. U.S. authorities have described the Feeding Our Future case as one of the largest fraud schemes in Minnesota’s history. Officials said Idle’s arrest underscores their commitment to pursuing individuals accused of financial crimes, regardless of where they attempt to evade justice. Idle is expected to face legal proceedings in connection with the charges brought against him in the United States. items.title: Daawo: Somalia oo Record caalami ah jebisey kadib markii…
items.description: London (Caasimada Online) – Dowladda Federaalka Soomaaliya aya maanta jebisey Recordkii cusub oo ku aadan heshiisyada caalamiga ah, kadib markii Hay’adda Baddaha Aduunka IMO ay ka diiwaangelisey 15 heshiis oo caalami ah. Wasiirka Wasaaradda Dekadaha iyo Gaadiidka Badda Mudane, Cabduqaadir Maxamed Nuur (Jaamac) oo hadda ku sugan magaalada London ee caasimada dalka Ingiriiska ayaa Xarunta Ururka Badaha Adduunka ee Qaramada Midoobay ka diiwaangeliyay heshiisyadan oo ay horay u meel-mariyeen xubnaa Golaha Wasiirrada Soomaaliya, isla markaana muhiim u ah dalka. Documentiyada la gubdiyay ayaa isugu jiro 15 heshiis, borotokool iyo lifaaqyo sharciyeed oo caalami ah oo la xiriira arrimaha badaha, iyadoo tallaabadan lagu tilmaamay mid lagu casriyeynayo hannaanka sharciyeed ee badaha dalka. Wasiir Jaamac oo faah-faahin ka bixiyay tallaabada ay qaadeen ayaa guul ku tilmaamay, wuxuuna sheegay in tani ay tahay isbeddelkii ugu ballaarnaa ee lagu sameeyo sharciyada badaha Soomaaliya tan iyo markii ay xornimada qaadatay Soomaaliya, isla markaana ay dalka ka caawin doonto inuu la jaanqaado xeerarka caalamiga ah ee khuseeya badqabka maraakiibta, amniga badda, heerarka badmaaxiinta iyo ilaalinta deegaanka badda. “Maanta waa maalin wayn oo taariikhi ah oo dalka iyo dadka Soomaaliyeed qiimo wayn ugu fadhido waa maalin aan soo diiwaangelinay 15 documenti oo dalka Soomaaliyeed, gaar ahaan inta daneysa arrimaha badda aan kusoo diiwaanelinay Hay’adda Badaha Caalamiga ah ee IMO waa maalin aan dhihi karno taariikhda weli kama dhicin in documintiyo heerkan la eeg ay dowladi keento xaruna IMO,” ayuu yiri Wasiir Cabdulqaadir Maxamed Nuur (Jaamac). Waxaa kale oo uu intaas kusii datay “Shuruucda aan diiwaangelinay waxay u adeegayaan oo ay muhiim u yihiin arrimaha diblumaasiyadda, ganacsiga, difaaca iyo ilaalinta gobonnimada dalka Soomaaliyeed”. In kasta oo Soomaaliya ay leedahay xeeb-barriyeedka ugu dheer Afrika, isla markaana ay ku taallo marinno istiraatiiji ah oo ka mid ah kuwa ugu muhiimsan adduunka, haddana tan iyo 1960-kii waxay ku biirtay oo keliya saddex heshiis oo caalami ah oo la xiriira arrimaha badaha, sida ay shaacisay Wasaaradda Dekadaha iyo Gaadiidka Badda ee Xukuumadda Soomaaliya. Si kastaba, ku biirista heshiisyadan waxay Soomaaliya ka dhigaysaa dal firfircoon oo ka tirsan nidaamka caalamiga ah ee badaha, iyadoo xoojinaysa badqabka iyo amniga badda, ilaalinta deegaanka, iyo hirgelinta heerarka caalamiga ah. Sidoo kale, waxay dhiirrigelinaysaa maalgashiga, kobcinta dhaqaalaha buluugga ah, iyo ballaarinta fursadaha ganacsi iyo iskaashiga caalamiga ah, taas oo ka tarjumaysa aragtida Dowladda Federaalka Soomaaliya ee ku aaddan horumarinta waarta ee howlaha qaran ee la xiriira badaha. The post Daawo: Somalia oo Record caalami ah jebisey kadib markii… appeared first on Caasimada Online .
